name: Exp A: Practical tirzepatide long-forms (Lane A)
hypothesis: Long-tail practical tirzepatide questions that people search for beat approved-drug deep dives and keep gaining views over time.
change: Lane A on every day without qualifying news, with the long-tail searched question first in the title.
metric: Success: day-7 median of 25+ views and 60+ watch minutes, still growing at day 28.
result: Won at n=8+ (How Long, What to Eat, Side Effects, Strength, Plateau, Bones & Muscle, Protein, Thanksgiving). The 4 mature videos got 51, 115, 126 and 141 views (median about 120) and 204, 273, 412 and 433 min (median about 340), vs about 38 min for the 11 other GLP-1 long-forms. That's about 9× more. Suggested videos bring about 68% of Lane A minutes, at 5–6 min per view. Caveat: Plateau (12 views, 87 impressions at day 5) and Bones & Muscle (10 views, 67 impressions at day 4) start slowly but hold 68–79% of the video. Protein reached 146 views by day 3. Lane A is now the default for every 14:00 long-form.

name: Exp B: Gray-market 'what's actually confirmed' long-forms
hypothesis: Our strongest Short lane would also work as long-form.
change: 2 long-forms a week in lane B.
result: Closed early at n=1: the pharmacy check got 8 views and 20 min before it closed (11 views and 31 min now). Gray-market stays Shorts-only, at most 1 a week.

name: Exp C: First explainer within 48 h of a new named result
hypothesis: Being the first clear explainer of a newly public named trial result drives more long-form views than evergreen topics.
change: The long-form slot went to qualifying fresh randomized results.
result: Retired without reaching its sample. Only 1 valid video in the window: petrelintide, with 30 views and 97 min, below the 50-view bar. The only qualifying news this week (retatrutide vs semaglutide, 10-29) was dropped for audio. Looking back at fresh next-gen results (n=7): median about 35 views and about 97 min. Only EloraTZP was big. Lane A median is about 340 min, so the cost of giving the slot to news is too high. News now goes to 13:00 Shorts. Only a randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide or semaglutide may get an extra L2 long-form.

name: Exp D: Shorts-to-long-form funnel with a verified link
hypothesis: A 20:00 Short that asks a fresh question a live long-form answers, with a verified description link, lifts that long-form's daily views.
change: New targets: the 20:00 Short now points to live Lane A long-forms with the most minutes per view (Hair Loss once it's live, What to Eat, Side Effects, Protein) instead of EloraTZP. Last line and publisher link are unchanged.
metric: The target long-form's viewCount in the 3 days after the Short vs the 3 days before, plus its SHORTS and RELATED_VIDEO traffic. Success: an average lift of 10+ views a day, or 50%+ over the per-video baseline.
min_sample: n=6 funnel Shorts with a verified working link
result: No valid data point is logged yet. SHORTS traffic is still 0 on all 20 long-forms with traffic data. The analyst must log the target and link status for every 20:00 Short from 11-03.

name: Exp E: State-change thumbnail on What to Eat
hypothesis: What to Eat has a packaging problem, not a discovery problem: 1,290 impressions at 2.79% CTR. A state-change thumbnail of 4 words or fewer will lift CTR toward the 3.8–5.0% our similar thumbnails get.
change: Only the thumbnail changes: a state-change design of 4 words or fewer, no body imagery. Use the owner's Test & Compare if available; otherwise the publisher swaps it via the API on 11-04. Title and description stay as they are for 14 days.
metric: CTR on new impressions and views per day, vs 2.79% and the 7 days before the swap. Success: CTR of 3.5%+ with views per day not falling.
min_sample: 1,000 new impressions or 14 days, whichever comes later
result: Starts 11-04. Baseline: 1,290 impressions, 2.79% CTR, 115 views, 433 min. Strength (2.68% on 1,155) is next, but only after E reads out, so we change one variable at a time.

name: Exp F: A benefit-framed subscribe line in Shorts
hypothesis: Shorts bring about 300 YouTube views a day but almost no subscribers (about 0.5 per 1,000). One honest line that names the channel's promise will at least double conversion.
change: On 08:00 and 13:00 Shorts only, the second-to-last spoken line is: 'We answer one tirzepatide question from the research every day. Subscribe if that helps.' 20:00 Shorts get no line and act as the same-day control. Nothing else changes.
metric: subscribersGained per 1,000 views at day 7: 08:00/13:00 Shorts vs 20:00 Shorts. Also channel subscribers per 1,000 YouTube views vs the 10-27→11-02 baseline of about 3.6 (8 subscribers on about 2,250 views). Success: 2× the control rate and 2.5+ channel subscribers a day.
min_sample: 14 days (about 28 Shorts with the line, 14 without)
result: Starts 11-03. Subscriber counts per Short are small, so read the 14-day totals, not single Shorts.
